reason: A sabre-shaped beak is flattened and curved like a sword blade, i.e. falcate; PATO:0002215 falciform has falcate and sickle-shaped as synonyms. PATO:0002235 blade-like (ensiform) is straight, so it fits less well.
'semi-' qualifies an existing value the way 'sub-' does (compare 'semi-canaliculate'); the value is FLOPO:0991108 climbing with value_qualifier approximately.
Muricate already means bearing minute hard pointed outgrowths; 'spinously' only says how sharp they are. 'on the keels' is the part of the glume (slot 1), not part of the quality.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: orbicular PATO_0001934 with value_qualifier approximately – spatulate PATO_0001937)
reason: A compound of two existing 2-D shape values, the first with 'sub-' (docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md).
Tetrangular (French 'tétragone') means four-angled in cross-section: PATO:0001988 quadrangular.

This describes movement in the wind that follows from long slender stalks (as in Briza), not a quality of the spikelet or leaflet itself; the stalk's length and slenderness carry the morphological information.
Members of a set of like parts (sepals, bracts) differ in size, here in width: FLOPO:0991101 unequal, which is a size quality of a set of parts.
PO already has the class unifacial vascular leaf (synonym unifacial leaf); 'leaf blade unifacial' places the leaf in that class rather than stating a quality.
Same as rule C349 'veinless': the complement of having a vein. The second example ('1veined') is a count and belongs in docs/odp/03-count-of-parts.md.
It means 'appearing in spring', a statement about season (phenology), not a quality of the leaf or inflorescence; it is out of scope for an entity–quality annotation.
A windowed fruit septum (perforated, as in some Brassicaceae) is fenestrate: PATO:0002064 fenestrated. The bearer is fruit septum (PO_0025268). The flower example ('in profile windowed') is unclear.
Negation of the existing colour value PATO:0000322 red, like 'unlobed' = not lobed.
States that the costa has no stereids: the complement of has_part some stereid (PO_0030045). 'in transverse section' is how the observation was made, not part of the quality.
A rounded leaf base is obtuse, as in the earlier answer for 'short-rounded'; 'abruptly' is a degree modifier. The bearer is the leaf base (slot 1).
The example is truncated, so it is not clear what is off-centre on the calyptra (beak or insertion). The word is meaningless without the part it describes.
A misspelling of areolate (spore wall divided into small areas): PATO:0002295; 'somewhat' is approximately (docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md).

target: new: conjunction of two qualities (angular PATO_0001977 and isometrical PATO_0001573)
reason: Cells that are both angular and isodiametric: two existing values that both apply. Isodiametric maps to PATO:0001573 isometrical (as in config/flora_union_pairs.tsv). The bearer is the exothecium cell (exothecium PO_0030073).
It names a kind of vein (veins running toward the margin) that has no PO or FLOPO class, and comes from two statements; 'veins present' alone would lose the meaning.

target: new: conjunction of two qualities (ascending PATO_0104355 and sinuous PATO_0001989) + docs/odp/06-specimen-condition.md
reason: Leaves that are both ascending and flexuous (flexuous = PATO:0001989 sinuous, rule C190); 'when dry' is the specimen condition.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (attached to PATO_0001667 towards peristome tooth PO_0030043)
reason: A relation to another part: the endostome segments are attached to the exostome teeth, which are peristome teeth (PO_0030043).
A transcription fragment without its object ('bearing persistent, shredded leaf bases'). The statement is really the presence of persistent leaf bases on the stem.
As in the earlier answer for 'broadly rhombic': rhomboid, with 'broad' as a degree. The bearer is the hyaline cell of the leaf, not the leaf.
Wedge-shaped is an EXACT synonym of PATO:0001955 cuneate; 'broadly' is a degree modifier.

In mosses the bud-like structure is the perigonium (the cluster of antheridia and leaves), not the antheridium. A comparison to a bud is too vague to be a shape term, and there are only two statements.
A part, not a quality. 'present' and 'lacking' are then the presence or absence of PO_0030051 in the stem.
A compound of two existing shape values; 'obloid' is the 3-D form of oblong.
'Leaves in tight, complex spirals' is a leaf arrangement: FLOPO:0991114 spirally arranged. 'Tight' and 'complex' add no class-level meaning.
'papillae compounded of blunt lobes' means the papillae are lobed (compound papillae). The bearer is the papilla (PO_0025166), also in the laminal-cell example.

An umbrella-shaped hypophysis (sporangium base PO_0030040) of Splachnaceae; no term for umbrella-shaped exists, and two statements do not justify a new one. 'convex' alone (PATO:0001355) would lose the meaning.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md slot 1 (base: heart shaped PATO_0000948; apex: acuminate PATO_0002228)
reason: Two values on different parts of the same organ: a cordate base and an acuminate apex. Each goes on its own part through slot 1; it is not a continuum.
